thread:
Samira: heads up — after yesterday's console rollout I'm seeing huge main-thread stalls when opening org dashboards, charts stutter badly
Rhea: yup noticed that too, especially on cold loads. flamegraphs show a lot of time in `serializeTelemetry` on the main thread
Ankit: was that the chunk-splitting PR? I thought it should reduce initial bundle size, not increase main-thread work
Samira: it did reduce bundle bytes, but we switched telemetry emission to synchronous JSON.stringify per widget mount. thousands of small calls now
Jo: that sounds like the culprit. can you paste the flame snippet?
Rhea: here — main thread spikes around 120–350ms where each widget does `emitTelemetry({type: 'widget-render', ...})` before mount completes
Rhea: ```
// simplified
function mountWidget() {
  reportTelemetry({event: 'widget-render', id}); // sync stringify + fetch
  render();
}
```
Ankit: oof. doing network+stringify on mount is rough. options: debounce/aggregate, move stringify to worker, or send light ping then batch payloads
Diego: +1 on batching. also curious if the chunk splitting moved some shared telemetry util into each chunk, so code duplicated per widget instance?
Samira: yeah we inadvertently inlined a small helper in 3 separate chunks, so the same logic runs independently in each bundle instance
Jo: two-level approach: 1) quick fix — debounce telemetry emission to next tick and batch with micro-batch window 100ms, 2) medium — web worker + structuredClone to offload stringify, 3) long — central telemetry service with small handshake then bulk upload
Rhea: for 1) can we just wrap current `emitTelemetry` with: `pending.push(payload); scheduleFlush()`? scheduleFlush uses rIC or setTimeout(50)
Ankit: schedule with requestIdleCallback fallback would be good, but rIC isn't reliable on mobile. setTimeout(50) + postMessage flush could work
Samira: does anyone worry about losing too much fidelity for QA/eval if we batch 50–100ms? metrics team needs per-widget timings for regressions
Jo: we can keep high-resolution local timestamps and include them in the batched payload. nothing prevents us from keeping accuracy while reducing stringify calls
Diego: agree. also we should dedupe the helper to avoid multiple copies — move to shared chunk or load from runtime global so there's only one stringify path
Samira: would a small perf test help? I'll open a canary with emit batching + shared helper and run synthetic dashboard opens (cold + warm)
Ankit: sounds good. on quotas: does this change alter telemetry volume? batching lowers number of requests but payload sizes increase — doesn't affect server rate limits but may affect payload-based billing
Rhea: for now backend accepts bulk arrays so no bill change. ops: we should inform backend about new endpoint `telemetry/bulk/v1` to allow better ingestion tuning
Jo: I'll file a short RFC for the bulk endpoint and retention semantics. can we also add a flag in Console rollout to disable client telemetry entirely for a specific canary? helps isolate perf impact during rollouts
Diego: there's already a `telemetryDisabled` remote flag used for experiments. we can toggle per-deployment. good call to include in rollout doc
Samira: quick plan: 1) revert inlined helper to shared module (PR today) 2) debounce batch (small PR) 3) canary with telemetryDisabled toggle and backend bulk endpoint stub 4) measure and iterate
Rhea: plz add perf numbers in PR description (TTI, main-thread time, first-contentful-paint) — makes review faster
Ankit: I'll help with the microbench harness. can we test with low-end laptop profile in lab?
Jo: yep I'll spin up the lab job, tag this thread when results are in
deploy-bot: deploy started for branch feature/chunk-split-telemetry-fix (build #6842) :rocket:
Samira: thanks — i'll watch the canary and report numbers here
Rhea: and if anyone hits this live: `localStorage.__telemetry_debug = 'off'` will temporarily silence client events for testing (not for prod use) :warning:
